描述_ZN: Axis of "Wu Rui Tu", Yongzheng, Qing dynasty, painted by Lang Shining, on silk with color, 140 cm long and 84 cm wide.　　This is a near-European still-life painting, with a celadon vase containing cattail leaves, pomegranate flowers, and marshmallow blossoms, a tray containing plums and cherries, and a few dumplings scattered about. The zongzi and the cattail in the picture suggest that the painting was painted for the Dragon Boat Festival, a traditional Chinese holiday. In terms of composition, the objects in the painting are clustered and scattered in a square triangular layout, giving a sense of stability to the human eye. The painting method uses shades of color and shadows to show the three-dimensionality of the flowers, fruits and vase, especially the "highlighting" technique on the shoulder of the vase, which is found in European paintings but not in Chinese paintings, so that the viewer can clearly appreciate the skills of Western oil painting. Although the picture is not dated, according to the archives of the Office of the Interior of the Qing Dynasty, it was painted in 1732, one of Lang Shining's early works in China.　　As an exotic visitor to China, the many missionaries who arrived in China in the late Ming and early Qing dynasties adopted the missionary strategy of blending Eastern and Western cultures and then implementing the doctrine in a gradual and progressive manner, and Lang Shining was undoubtedly a thorough practitioner. Although his technique of representing still life in this painting is derived from European oil paintings, its content reflects the customs of the Chinese people, which have been embodied in the essence of their culture for more than two thousand years. It was his eclectic technique of combining Chinese and foreign knowledge and his choice of subject matter to suit the interests of the Chinese emperors that made Lang Shining a Western painter who was highly appreciated and greatly used by the Yongzheng and Qianlong emperors, and to which he owes the survival of a large number of his paintings.　　Signed: "Painted by Lang Shining", with two seals, the inscriptions indistinct. The seal of the connoisseurship collection reads, "A treasure of the Qianlong imperial court".
